svg.title: Checked Ethernet, IPv4, UDP and ARP boundaries
svg.desc: Offsets are bytes from destination MAC. Ethernet header is bytes zero through thirteen. IPv4 total length bounds the IP region; IHL locates UDP and UDP length bounds payload. Trailing Ethernet padding is excluded. A second row gives Ethernet IPv4 ARP field offsets.

g.text: Read a field only after its containing region fits
Example: untagged IPv4, no options, eight-byte HFS message. All offsets in bytes.
Destination MAC
Source MAC
EtherType
IPv4 header
UDP header
HFS payload
IP total length = 36; must fit within captured_length − 14
UDP length = 16 = IP total length − IHL × 4
IPv4: byte 14 version/IHL; 16–17 total length; 20–21 flags/fragment offset;
23 protocol (17 = UDP); 26–29 source IP; 30–33 destination IP.
UDP: 34–35 source port; 36–37 destination port; 38–39 length; 40–41 checksum.
Options shift UDP to 14 + IHL × 4. Never hardcode offset 34 in the decoder.
Bytes after 14 + IP total length are outside IP (for example, Ethernet padding).
Separate ARP branch — EtherType 0x0806, at least 42 captured bytes
14–15 hardware type 1; 16–17 protocol 0x0800; 18 MAC size 6; 19 IP size 4;
20–21 opcode 1 request / 2 reply; 22–27 sender MAC; 28–31 sender IPv4;
32–37 target MAC; 38–41 target IPv4. No IPv4 header or UDP header here.
Capture starts at destination MAC: normally no preamble/start delimiter or FCS. Veth is software only.
